source_text:
{ΚΥΡ.} Τί δὲ, οἱ παθῶν ἀμείνους, καὶ νεκροῦντες τὰ μέλη τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, πορνείαν, ἀκαθαρσίαν, πάθος, ἐπιθυμίαν κακὴν, οὐκ εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας ἀνακείσονται τῷ Θεῷ, καὶ ἐν τάξει τῶν ὁλοκαυτωμάτων εἶεν ἂν, λύτρον ὥσπερ τι, καὶ ἐξιλασμὸν ὑπέρ γε τῶν ἰδίων ψυχῶν τὸ χρῆμα ποιούμενοι·
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Καὶ μάλα.
{ΚΥΡ.} Ἡμέραν τοίνυν ἐξιλασμοῦ τὴν τῆς ἀσιτίας ὁ νομοθέτης ὠνόμαζε, καὶ σφόδρα ὀρθῶς καὶ ἐννόμως, κατανεκρῶν μὲν τὴν σάρκα καὶ τὰ αὐτῆς, εὐωδιάζων δὲ δὴ τῆς ἀρετῆς τοὺς τρόπους. Ἔργου δὲ παντὸς μὴ καταλήγων κοσμικοῦ, πάντη τε καὶ πάντως ἐν ἐσχάτοις ἔσται κακοῖς, ὃ παρέδειξεν ἐναργῶς, ἐξολοθρευθήσεσθαι λέγων ἐκ τοῦ λαοῦ αὐτοῦ τὸν μήτε νηστεύοντα, μήτε μὴν προσάγοντα τὴν ὁλοκαύτωσιν, καὶ τὸν ἐπὶ ταῖς ἀργίαις περιυβρίζοντα νόμον. Σάββατα δὲ σαββάτων τὸν ἐπὶ τοῖσδε καιρὸν εἶναι λέγων, ἐφῆκε νοεῖν, ὡς ἔστι λοιπὸν ἀργιῶν ἀργία, τουτέστιν, ὁλοτελῶς καὶ ὡς ἐν ὁλοκλήρῳ μέτρῳ τῶν ἔργων ἀπόθεσις, δῆλον δὲ ὅτι τῶν εἰς φαυλότητά τε καὶ ἁμαρτίαν. Καταλήγοντος δὲ τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου, καὶ μονονουχὶ καταγηράσκοντος τοῦ καιροῦ, μοίραν ὅλως ἐν ἡμῖν ποίαν ἂν ἔχοι λοιπὸν ἡ εἰς ματαιότητα σπουδὴ καὶ οὐχὶ δὴ μᾶλλον τὰ ἀμείνω φρονήσομεν, τὴν τῷ Θεῷ θυμηρεστάτην ἐπιτελοῦντες ἀργίαν, καὶ τῶν οἰκείων περισπασμῶν ἀποφοιτῶντες εἰσάπαν;
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Εὖ λέγεις.
{ΚΥΡ.} Θεσμοθετεῖ δὲ δὴ πάλιν· «Καὶ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ, φησὶ, τῇ πεντεκαιδεκάτῃ τοῦ μηνὸς τοῦ ἑβδόμου τούτου, ὅταν συντελέσητε τὰ γεννήματα τῆς γῆς, ἑορτάσατε τῷ Κυρίῳ ἑπτὰ ἡμέρας. Τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ πρώτῃ ἀνάπαυσις, καὶ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ὀγδόῃ ἀνάπαυσις, καὶ λήψεσθε τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ πρώτῃ καρπὸν ξύλου ὡραῖον, καὶ κάλλυντρα φοινίκων, καὶ κλάδους ξύλου δασεῖς, καὶ ἰτέας, καὶ ἄγνου κλάδους ἐκ χειμάῤῥου, καὶ εὐφρανθήσεσθε ἔναντι Κυρίου τοῦ Θεοῦ ὑμῶν ἑπτὰ ἡμέρας τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ, νόμιμον αἰώνιον εἰς τὰς γενεὰς ὑμῶν. Ἐν τῷ μηνὶ τῷ ἑβδόμῳ ἑορτάσετε αὐτήν.» Ἆρ' αἰσθάνῃ τε λοιπὸν, ὅτι συναγηγερμένων εἰς ἀποθήκην τῶν ἐν ἀγροῖς, καὶ συνειλεγμένων εὖ μάλα τῶν ἑκάστου καρπῶν, ἀγχοῦ δὴ λίαν ἡ παναοίδιμος ἑορτὴ τῆς Σκηνοπηγίας, τὴν ἐν παραδείσῳ δίαιταν ὑποφαίνουσα· καὶ τῶν ἐν ἀρχαῖς εἰς μέθεξιν ἀνατιθεῖσα τὸν ἄνθρωπον. Φαμὲν γὰρ εἶναι Σκηνοπηγίαν, τὴν νοητὴν καὶ ἀληθεστέραν τῶν ἀνθρωπίνων σωμάτων τὴν σύμπηξιν, καὶ τὸ ἐκ τῆς διὰ μέσου φθορᾶς ἀναβιῶναι εἰς ἀφθαρσίαν. Ἀνάπαυσις δὲ ἡ πρώτη καὶ μέν τοι καὶ ἡ ὀγδόη· πρὸ γάρ τοι τῆς ἐν ἀρχαῖς παραβάσεως, οὔπω τῆς μοχθηροτάτης ἡμῖν ἐμβαλούσης ἁμαρτίας, καὶ τὸν δυσαχθῆ καὶ δυσδιακόμιστον ἀληθῶς ἐπιτιθείσης ζυγὸν, ἀνειμένην τινὰ καὶ ἄφετον, καὶ δίχα πόνου παντὸς τὴν ἐν παραδείσῳ δίαιταν ἐποιούμεθα, καθάπερ ἐν ἀρχῇ καὶ ῥίζῃ τοῦ γένους ἐν Ἀδάμ. Ἐπιδημήσαντος δὲ τοῦ Χριστοῦ, καὶ τὸ διὰ μέσου εἰς πόνους, ἀνέδραμεν εἰς τὸ ἐν ἀρχαῖς κατὰ τὴν ὀγδόην, τουτέστι, μετὰ τὸν ἐν νόμῳ σαββα
pass_a_gloss: CYR.: And what, those better than passions, and deadening the members on the earth, fornication, uncleanness, passion, evil desire, will they not be dedicated into a smell of sweet savor to God, and would they be in the rank of the whole burnt offerings, making the matter as it were a ransom and propitiation on behalf of their own souls? PALL.: Very much. CYR.: Then the lawgiver named the day of fasting a day of propitiation, and very rightly and lawfully, deadening the flesh and its things, and making fragrant the ways of virtue. And the one not ceasing from every worldly work will be altogether and in every way in the last evils, which he showed clearly, saying that the one neither fasting nor bringing the whole burnt offering, and the one insulting the law on the days of rest, will be utterly destroyed from his people. And saying the time on these to be sabbaths of sabbaths, he left it to be understood that there is for the rest an idleness of idlenesses, that is, wholly and as in complete measure the putting-off of the works, plainly those toward baseness and sin. And this age ceasing, and the time all but growing old, what portion at all would the zeal for vanity have among us for the rest, and will we not rather think the better things, accomplishing the idleness most pleasing to God, and departing altogether from our own distractions? PALL.: You say well. CYR.: And he lays down law again: 'And on the day', he says, 'the fifteenth of this seventh month, whenever you complete the produce of the land, keep feast to the Lord seven days. On the first day a rest, and on the eighth day a rest, and you will take on the first day fruit of a tree beautiful, and fronds of palms, and thick branches of tree, and willows, and branches of chaste-tree from a torrent, and you will be gladdened before the Lord your God seven days of the year, lasting ordinance into your generations. In the seventh month you will keep it as feast.' Do you perceive then for the rest that, the things in the fields having been gathered into a storehouse, and the crops of each having been collected very well, very near indeed the all-sung feast of the Tent-pitching, hinting the way of life in paradise, and setting man into participation of the things at the beginnings. For we say the Tent-pitching to be the spiritual and truer joining-together of the human bodies, and the coming back to life from the corruption in between into incorruption. And a rest the first and indeed also the eighth; for before the transgression at the beginnings, the most wicked sin not yet having fallen on us, and having laid the heavy and truly hard-to-carry yoke, we made the way of life in paradise loosed and free and apart from every toil, as in a beginning and root of the race in Adam. But Christ having come to dwell, also the in-between into toils ran up into the thing at the beginnings according to the eighth, that is, after the sabbath (-keeping) in the law (continues)
pass_b_english: Cyril: Well then, will not those who are above the passions, and who put to death the members that are on the earth, fornication, impurity, passion, evil desire (Colossians 3:5), be dedicated to God as a fragrant odor and stand in the rank of the whole burnt offerings, making the matter a kind of ransom and propitiation for their own souls?

Cyril: So the lawgiver called the day of fasting the Day of Atonement, and very rightly and lawfully, since it puts to death the flesh and what belongs to it and makes the ways of virtue fragrant. And whoever does not cease from all worldly work will be, utterly and in every way, in the worst of evils. This he showed clearly by saying that whoever neither fasts nor offers the whole burnt offering, and whoever outrages the law about the days of rest, will be destroyed from his people. And by saying that the time for these things is a sabbath of sabbaths, he left us to understand that there is from now on a rest of rests, that is, a laying aside of works wholly and in full measure, plainly of works that lead to wickedness and sin. And now that this age is coming to its close and the time is all but growing old, what share at all could the pursuit of vanity still have in us? Shall we not rather set our minds on better things, keeping the rest most pleasing to God and withdrawing entirely from our own distractions?

Cyril: And again he lays down the law: ‘And on the fifteenth day,’ it says, ‘of this seventh month, when you have finished gathering the produce of the land, keep a feast to the Lord seven days. On the first day there shall be a rest, and on the eighth day a rest. And on the first day you shall take the beautiful fruit of a tree, and branches of palms, and thick boughs of trees, and willows, and branches of chaste-tree from the brook; and you shall rejoice before the Lord your God seven days in the year. It is a perpetual ordinance throughout your generations. In the seventh month you shall keep it’ (Leviticus 23:39–41).

Do you perceive, then, that when the produce of the fields has been gathered into the storehouse and each man's crops have been well collected, the far-famed Feast of Tabernacles is very near, hinting at the life in paradise and restoring man to a share in what was at the beginning? For we say that the Feast of Tabernacles is the spiritual and truer joining-together of human bodies, and their return to life out of the corruption that came between, into incorruption. And the first day is a rest, and so is the eighth. For before the transgression at the beginning, when the most wicked sin had not yet fallen upon us and laid on us its yoke, truly heavy and hard to bear, we led a life in paradise that was free and unbound and without any toil, as in Adam, the beginning and root of the race. But when Christ came to dwell among us, the time of toil that came between ran back to what was at the beginning on the eighth day, that is, after the law’s…

choices.term: τὴν νοητὴν καὶ ἀληθεστέραν τῶν ἀνθρωπίνων σωμάτων τὴν σύμπηξιν
choices.english: the spiritual and truer joining-together of human bodies
choices.why: σύμπηξις plays on σκηνοπηγία ('tent-pitching'): the body as a tent pitched again in the resurrection.

choices.english: a sabbath of sabbaths ... a rest of rests
